In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Commentary on Surat al-Ma'arij

It is a Meccan surah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall﴾, meaning: "that is to befall" — i.e., a caller called out.

The verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah, and he said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment." So this verse was revealed.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿with a punishment that is to befall﴾ — the "bi" (ba') is extra (silah).

Its meaning: a caller called out, and one seeking it asked for a punishment from Allah, exalted is He.

His saying: ﴿wāqi'﴾ — meaning: existing and occurring with respect to the disbelievers. That is the Day of Resurrection, when this punishment will certainly befall them.

It has also been said: it refers to this world, and that punishment did befall al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, when he was killed in cold blood on the Day of Badr.

This which we have mentioned is the meaning according to Mujahid and others.

The second opinion regarding the verse: "A questioner asked about a punishment that is to befall" — the "bi" (ba') is in the sense of "'an" (about), as said by al-Farra' and others.

The meaning: a questioner asked: "On whom will the punishment fall? And upon whom will the punishment descend?"

Then God Most High said: ﴿for the disbelievers﴾, meaning: upon the disbelievers.

It is recited, as an irregular reading (shadh): "sāla sā'il" (سَالَ سَائل). It is said: sāla is used with the meaning of sa'ala (سَأَلَ), with the hamza dropped.

It was also said: sāla sā'il means: a valley in Hell that flows upon the disbelievers with punishment.

As for the words of God Most High: ﴿there is none to avert it﴾, meaning: no one can avert the punishment from the disbelievers, nor can anyone prevent it from reaching them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾, meaning: Lord of the heavens. The heavens are called ma'arij (ascending stairways) because the angels ascend (ya'rujun) to them.

It is also said: dhu al-ma'arij means dhu al-fawadil (Lord of the bounties).

It is also said: dhu al-darajat (Lord of the degrees), in the sense of His honouring the believers with degrees and giving them to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾. We have already explained the meaning of the Spirit (al-ruh).

It is also said: they are in the creation of the heaven, resembling the children of Adam, though they are not children of Adam.

And His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the Day of Resurrection, and it is the more correct of the two opinions.

Al-Hasan related it as a mursal report, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri related it as a musnad report in some rare narrations: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, will lighten it for the believers, so that it will be equal to the prayer of an obligatory prayer performed lightly."

And in some reports: "As much as the time between noon and the afternoon."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: from the floor of the earth to above the Throne is fifty thousand years.

It is also said that the meaning of His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ is: even if a worker worked, or a reckoner reckoned, what Allah does in one hour or in one day would not come to an end within fifty thousand years.

And it is related from Ibn 'Abbas in some narrations that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, and His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count﴾, are two verses whose meaning none knows except Allah.

The same is related from Qatadah.

And His saying: as for His saying ﴿a thousand years﴾, it is the distance between the heaven and the earth, going up and coming down.

And His saying: ﴿fifty thousand years﴾ is the distance between the earth and the Throne, going up.

And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿So be patient with gracious patience﴾, meaning: patience without anxiety (jaza') and without complaint (shakwa).

And from Qays ibn al-Hajjaj, regarding His saying: ﴿So be patient with gracious patience﴾, he said: It is that the one afflicted by the calamity is among the people and it is not known who he is. He was only commanded to be patient because the polytheists were harming him, so He commanded him to be patient until His punishment descends upon them.
"And His saying: ﴿Indeed they see it as distant﴾, meaning: the punishment."

[Translation of the passage:]

And His saying: ﴿And We see it as near﴾ — because it is certain to occur and will undoubtedly come to pass.

God Almighty's words: ﴿On the Day when the sky will be like molten metal dregs﴾. That is, like the sediment of olive oil. It is also said: like the pitch of tar.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: It is what is melted from the essences of the earth, such as copper, lead and silver; all of them are called mahl.
And His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool(al-ʿihn)﴾. Al-ʿihn is dyed wool, and He likened them to it in their weakness and softness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 10:

And His saying: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend﴾. That is: no relative will ask about the condition of his relative, due to being preoccupied with himself.

It was also recited: "And no intimate friend will ask an intimate friend" (wa-la yas'alu ḥamīmun ḥamīman), meaning: no one will ask, "Where is your intimate friend?"

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 11–12:

And His saying: ﴿They will see them﴾ means: they will recognize them.

Its meaning: each of them will recognize the other, and will not ask him about his condition, being occupied with himself.

It has also been said: each of them will recognize the other by the marks and signs, for the people of Paradise have marks and signs, and likewise the people of the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿The criminal would wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his sons, and his companion (wife), and his brother﴾ — "companion" means his wife.

﴿And his brother﴾ is the well-known brother.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 11–12:

And His saying: ﴿They will see them﴾ means: they will recognize them.

Its meaning: each of them will recognize the other, and will not ask him about his condition, being occupied with himself.

It has also been said: each of them will recognize the other by the marks and signs, for the people of Paradise have marks and signs, and likewise the people of the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿The criminal would wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his sons, and his companion (wife), and his brother﴾ — "companion" means his wife.

﴿And his brother﴾ is the well-known brother.

And His saying: ﴿And his kinsfolk who shelter him﴾, that is, his tribe to which he resorts for refuge. It is also said: his nearest relatives.

Al-fasilah (the closest kin, lineage) is more immediate and nearer than the fahl (the paternal line / the lineage of a man's own stock).

And it is said: al-'Abbas is of the fasilah (close kin) of the Messenger.

And His saying: ﴿and all who are on the earth, together, then that it might deliver him﴾ means: even if he were to ransom himself with everyone on the earth, all together, in order to be saved, he would not be saved.

And His saying: ﴿Never!﴾ is as we have already explained the meaning.

It is narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdullah, the freedman of Ghafra, that every instance of "kallā" (never/no) in the Qur'an carries the sense of "you have lied" (kadhabta).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is Laẓā﴾ is a name among the names of Jahannam (Hellfire).

It is also said: "Indeed, it is Laẓā" means a constant punishment, from which no one will ever escape.

The Qur'anic phrase ﴿Tearing away at the extremities﴾ (nazza'atan lil-shawa).

Most commentators hold that al-shawa (the extremities) refers to the limbs, such as the two hands, the two feet, and so on.

Al-Farra' mentioned that it refers to the skin of the head.

It was also said: the skull (qahf al-ra's).

It is said: the skin and flesh, until only the bone remains.

It was also said: the skin, flesh and bone, until it reaches the heart, and it is scorched; this was related by Mujahid.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 17:

And His saying: ﴿It calls out to him who turned his back and withdrew﴾, that is: it calls out to the disbelievers who turned their backs and withdrew, saying, "O so-and-so," mentioning his name: "Come to me," and it seizes him.

Al-Mubarrad said regarding His saying ﴿tad'u﴾ (it calls out): that is, it punishes.

It is narrated from al-Nadr, from al-Khalil, that he heard a Bedouin say to another: "May God call you (da'aaka Allah)," meaning: may God punish you.

As for Tha'lab, he said: it calls them one by one by their names.

And this is the most apparent (al-azhar).

And His saying: ﴿And gathered [wealth] and hoarded it﴾. That is: he gathered wealth and stored it away, i.e., he placed it in a container and tied its mouth shut over it. This is a metaphor (kinayah) for stinginess and withholding what is owed.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious﴾. That is, prone to impatience (jaza').

Tha'lab said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Tahir asked me about this verse, and I said: al-hala' (the word hal'a) is the worst kind of jaza' (impatience).

It is also said: halu'an means distressed and restless (dajir).

And from al-Hasan: weak (da'if).

Al-Dahhak said: stingy (bakhil).

And from others: greedy (haris).

Tafsir al-Qur'an by al-Sam'ani, on surah 70, verses 20–21:

It is also said that its explanation is His saying: ﴿When evil touches him, he is anxious and distressed; and when good touches him, he is grudging and withholding.﴾ That is: when evil touches him, he does not show patience, and when good touches him, he does not give thanks.

Tafsir al-Qur'an by al-Sam'ani, on surah 70, verses 20–21:

It is also said that its explanation is His saying: ﴿When evil touches him, he is anxious and distressed; and when good touches him, he is grudging and withholding.﴾ That is: when evil touches him, he does not show patience, and when good touches him, he does not give thanks.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 70, verses 22–23:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who observe their prayer, who are constant in it﴾. This exception is taken as relating back to the beginning of the speech, and its meaning is that these people will be saved from the punishment.

Sufyan narrated from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: the verse refers to the obligatory prayers (al-salawat al-maktubah).

It has also been said: its constancy (idamah) is its establishment (iqamah) at its appointed times.

And it is said: its constancy is not that one prays all the time, but that when one prays, one does not turn right or left.

And it is said: the constancy of the prayers is that one does not abandon them, and this is a good view (qawl hasan).

And from some of the early generation (salaf): it is that one does not delay them beyond their times. As for one who abandons them, he is a disbeliever (kafir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 70, verses 22–23:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who observe their prayer, who are constant in it﴾. This exception is taken as relating back to the beginning of the speech, and its meaning is that these people will be saved from the punishment.

Sufyan narrated from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: the verse refers to the obligatory prayers (al-salawat al-maktubah).

It has also been said: its constancy (idamah) is its establishment (iqamah) at its appointed times.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 24–25:

And His saying: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right for the beggar﴾. This is the wanderer who asks (from) people.

And His saying: ﴿and the deprived﴾. It is the one who does not ask. It is said: he is the muharraf (the one whose livelihood has been diminished, the impoverished), and it is said: he is the mahdud (the one who has been cut off from provision).

Both have one meaning.

It is said: So-and-so is majdud, and So-and-so is mahdud. The majdud is the one whom good fortune (al-jadd) accompanies, and the mahdud is the deprived.

Ibn Umar said: "The deprived is the dog."

And from al-Sha'bi, he said: "I was unable to know the meaning of the deprived."

It is also said: he is the poor man who has nothing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 24–25:

And His saying: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right for the beggar﴾. This is the wanderer who asks (from) people.

And His saying: ﴿and the deprived﴾. It is the one who does not ask. It is said: he is the muharraf (the one whose livelihood has been diminished, the impoverished), and it is said: he is the mahdud (the one who has been cut off from provision).

Both have one meaning.

It is said: So-and-so is majdud, and So-and-so is mahdud. The majdud is the one whom good fortune (al-jadd) accompanies, and the mahdud is the deprived.

Ibn Umar said: "The deprived is the dog."

And from al-Sha'bi, he said: "I was unable to know the meaning of the deprived."

It is also said: he is the poor man who has nothing.
And His saying: ﴿And those who affirm the Day of Judgment﴾, i.e., they believe in it.

And His saying: ﴿And those who are apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord﴾, i.e., those who fear.

It is narrated on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: "Where are those who feared?" They will be gathered in the shelter of the Most Merciful, and Allah will not veil Himself from them.

Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris mentioned this in his tafsir.

And in the well-known report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, relating from Allah, the Exalted: "I do not combine for My servant two fears or two securities. If he fears Me in the world, I will grant him security on the Day of Resurrection; and if he feels secure from Me in the world, I will make him fear on the Day of Resurrection."
"His saying: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be deemed safe.﴾ The meaning is apparent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 29–30:

And His saying: ﴿And those who guard their chastity, except from their wives or those whom their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy﴾. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Whoever blames anyone for what his right hand possesses, even if it is many, or blames him regarding his wives when he has reached four, has disobeyed God the Exalted, because of His saying the Exalted: ﴿for then they are not blameworthy﴾. He also said: Whoever marries [four] women, or takes concubines from among the slave women, there is no flaw in his renunciation of the world, for 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, died leaving four free wives [and nineteen] concubines, and he was the most ascetic of the Companions.

In the verse there is evidence for the prohibition of temporary marriage (mut'ah).

'A'ishah was asked about temporary marriage and she said: "Between me and you is the Book of God," and she recited this verse.

Ibn 'Umar was asked about this and he said: "It is fornication (zina)."

It was said: "So-and-so permits it." He said: "Will you not stop muttering about it? In the time of 'Umar, by God, if he had caught him doing it, he would have stoned him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 29–30:

Qur'anic quotations are kept with ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translating:

And His saying: ﴿Whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors﴾ is evidence for what we have explained.

And "al-ʿadi" (the transgressor) and "al-mutaʿadi" (the transgressor) are one and the same.

And His words: ﴿And those who are, for their trusts and their covenant, keepers﴾. That is: guardians.

It has been said: the origin of the trust (amanah, that which is entrusted) is that the word of monotheism (tawhid, the affirmation of God's oneness), Allah the Exalted entrusted the believers with it.

And His words: ﴿And those who stand firm in their testimonies﴾. It is also recited as "bishahadatihim" (in their testimonies, plural). The one reading is in the sense of the plural (collective), and the other is in the sense of the singular (as a noun of unity).

The meaning of ﴿stand firm﴾ is: they discharge them (their testimonies) in their proper form.
And His saying: ﴿And those who are steadfast in their prayers﴾. We have already explained the meaning.
And His saying: ﴿Those will be in gardens, honored.﴾ That is: gardens in which Allah honors them with various kinds of blessings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 36:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So what is it with those who disbelieve, hastening towards you, [O Muhammad]?﴾ That is: rushing (muhti'in), hurrying.

Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas (d. 338 AH) said: The verse is problematic in meaning, and the intended meaning, Allah knows best, is: "What is the matter with those who disbelieve that they rush towards you to listen to the Qur'an, and then disperse without accepting it and believing in it?"

In the tafsir (narrations) it is said: They would come and sit around the Prophet (ﷺ) and look at him with the look of hatred and enmity, and listen to the Qur'an with the listening of mockery and denial.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 37:

And His saying: ﴿Coming from the right and from the left, in groups﴾ means: scattered, circle after circle.

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to the mosque while his Companions were scattered, each group in a place of its own, and he said: "What is the matter with me that I see you in groups?"

The Sunnah is that they sit in one circle, or some of them behind others, and that they do not scatter in their sitting.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Does every one of them hope to enter a Garden of bliss?﴾ The exegetes (al-mufassirun, the scholars of Qur'anic commentary) said: When God, exalted is He, mentioned Paradise for the believers, the disbelievers said: "We too will enter along with you;"

Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Nay﴾, meaning: the matter is not as they hope and presume.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created them from that which they know﴾, meaning: from filth and impurities.

The meaning is that entry into Paradise is not granted merely because one has been created, since he was created from something impure and filthy, so he does not deserve to enter Paradise. Rather, one deserves to enter Paradise through piety (taqwa) and religion (din).

It is also said: "We created them for the sake of what they know," meaning: the worship of Allah and belief in Him.

The poet said:

(Have you resolved to depart from the family of Layla in haste, and has she distanced herself, so that she would not visit the one who is in love?)

Meaning: "for the sake of the family of Layla."

It has also been said: ﴿Indeed, We created them from that which they know﴾ means "from those who know," i.e., "from among those who know."

The more correct view is the first.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 40–41:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾. Its meaning: "I swear" (uqsim), and this is according to the way of the Arabs, for they used to say it in this manner.

Here He mentioned "the easts and the wests" because the sun rises every day from a place other than the one it rose from on the first day, and likewise it sets from another place.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is related that it rises each day from a different aperture (kuwwa) and sets from a different aperture.

His words: ﴿Indeed We are able to replace them with better than them﴾, that is: more obedient to God than them, and more excellent than them.

His words: ﴿And We are not to be outdone﴾, that is: not to be prevented (mu'ajizin), and this has been explained before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verses 40–41:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾. Its meaning: "I swear" (uqsim), and this is according to the way of the Arabs, for they used to say it in this manner.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 42:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So leave them to plunge in vain talk and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection.

And it is mentioned as a threat, not as a permission or license given without restriction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 43:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day they come out from the graves swiftly﴾ mean: from the graves. Al-jadath (the grave) is the grave, and al-ajdath is its plural.

And His words: ﴿as if they were rushing toward a idol-stone, hastening﴾ mean: they come out swiftly, as if they were hastening toward a marked stone set up for them. It has been read as "nusubin yufdun" with a damma on the nun. Al-nusub and al-nasab have the same meaning, idols. They used to hasten toward their idols when they went to them, venerate them and touch them (for blessing).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 70, verse 44:

And His saying: ﴿Their eyes downcast﴾, meaning: their eyes will be humbled. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾, meaning: abasement.

And His saying: ﴿That is the Day which they were promised﴾, meaning: it will be said to them: "This is the Day that you were promised in the worldly life."

And Allah knows best.
